references.text: Pharaoh issues an expanded command to kill all male infants by casting them into the Nile, following up on the order given to the midwives.
Moses' mother hides him to prevent him from being killed in accordance with Pharaoh's decree to slay male children.
Herod's killing of the boys in Bethlehem parallels Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew male infants.
Stephen refers to how Pharaoh acted wickedly toward the Israelites, forcing them to expose their infants so they would die.
The Letter to the Hebrews mentions that Moses was hidden by his parents for three months because they did not fear the king's decree, referring to this command.
The term for birthstools (אָבְנָיִם) is also used here at Rachel's childbirth, pointing to the same birthing practice.
Ironical contrast: Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew boys meets God's judgment on his own firstborn.
Thematic parallel: Systematic violence against infants and pregnant women as a threat to God's people.
